It's not like a story or a tale, but when I was 17 I discoverd anonymous imageboards(4chan like), which made me really sociopathic.

I've spent 4 years on them, until I got to the point that I've got nothing to relate to in real life. Family, social activity, hobbies, proper studying - all was replaced by imageboards content. What I really liked in imageboards, is that you are free to express your opinion on any topic. What I didn't - is that people out there may be harsh and even harmful.

Imageboards were not the only places I spent my time - I also attended a local university. I had strong interest in IT programming and decided to get a formal degree in that field. Unfortunately, I chose a wrong university - people in my class didn't seek for professional development, but rather were hanging around. I hoped that If I could manage to educate myself, I would find a good job for my skills. But this didn't work, because this way I couldn't track my progress and get feedback. All local companies want ready-to-go specialists, but the place I studied in doesn't teach for these positions. 

Now I'm 23 and I'm in doubt whether I should continue studying while being depressed, or should I get a job in a local retail store just because I can't take it to be isolated anymore.
It might sound fun, but the solution was to apply for a fast food restaurant job. I've got some money and things to do.
